front: What is an **adjustment** at the year end?
back: An entry that corrects trial balance figures so that profit and the statement of financial position reflect the period; every adjustment has two sides.
Matching (accruals): revenue and costs belong to the period in which they arise, not when cash moves.

front: Charge for irrecoverable debts in the statement of profit or loss
back: Debts written off + increase (or - decrease) in the allowance. The allowance is calculated on receivables after the write-off.

front: Entry for goods taken by the owner
back: Debit drawings, credit purchases, at cost. Closing inventory is not changed.
Accrued expenses, depreciation, irrecoverable debts and increases in the allowance, and income received in advance.
Prepaid expenses, accrued income, goods taken by the owner and capital items wrongly charged as expenses.
A worksheet adding adjustment, profit or loss and financial position columns to the trial balance so the statements can be prepared directly.

front: Profit as the balancing figure in the extended trial balance
back: Debit side of the profit or loss columns and credit side of the financial position columns; a loss is the reverse.

front: Effect of a capital item charged as an expense
back: Expenses overstated and profit understated; the asset is missing. Correct it by capitalising and depreciating it.
